passage:
Each tree in the school garden received a name tag. The tags showed the tree's common name, scientific name, and a short fact.
Before the tags, most students said, "That tree" or "the big one near the wall." After the tags, they began saying "camphor tree" and "maple."
A student asked why names mattered. The biology teacher said, "When people know the name of something, they often notice it more."
The teacher was right. Students began comparing leaves and looking for flowers. Some even brought their parents to see the trees.
The trees had not changed. The students' attention had. A name can turn background into something seen.
